title: Development and evaluation of crowns for interference-free masticatory force measurement using microsensor technology (Smart Crown)
summary: As part of this pilot study (proof of concept), n = 2 study participants with need for a single crown in the posterior region and sufficient space are being sought. The plan is to attach one Smart Crown to a natural tooth and one to a dental implant. After taking an impression of the oral situation (geometry of the prepared tooth stump or implant position), the Smart Crowns are designed, manufactured and assembled in the laboratory, then tried in on the patient and adjusted if necessary. Finally, the crowns are permanently cemented. The force events exerted by the study participants on the Smart Crown will be recorded, stored and evaluated for at least one week.  At the same time, a “patient diary” will be kept in order to relate the measured chewing forces to the activities performed (e.g. eating).

interventions.name: Measurement of masticatory forces by use of microsensor technology integrated in a dental crown

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Need of a crown for a posterior tooth
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, lactant mothers, reasons against prosthetic treatment
